Senses.Explanation: Zen work while seated is the bounded physical use supported by retained records, not the name of a generic contemplative exercise. Guting Shanjian connects prolonged upright sitting with the work taught by the ancients, while Nanyue Huairang, Linji Yixuan, Baozhi, Zhaoqing Shengdeng, and Zhanran Yuancheng criticize taking sitting, gathered thought, timed concentration, or bodily form as the Way. The Baizhang code supplies only an institutional seating orientation in the hall. These witnesses establish sitting and Zen work in context; they do not supply a generic mental technique or make posture the meaning of 禪.

AlternateTargets: sitting Zen not confined to sitting
Senses.Note: Zen records explicitly redefine 坐 and 禪 or deny that 禪 is sitting or lying; this is the controlling Zen-record use.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The complete source explicitly names Fu Dashi as actor of this unit.

Senses.Explanation: Sitting Zen beyond bodily posture is the explicit redefinition preserved in Zen records. Huineng says that toward outside good and bad circumstances thoughts not arising is named 坐, while inwardly seeing one's own nature unmoved is named 禪. Nanyue Huairang tells Mazu that 禪 is not sitting or lying, and Fu Dashi writes of 坐禪 while lying down all day. The compound therefore cannot be reduced to a generic contemplative exercise: these uses make bodily posture nonessential and point to Zen rather than a generic contemplative exercise.
